verdict.summary: There's no app review: create an app in the Developer Console, set callback URLs and go, and any X user can authorize the same day. But since February 2026 the API is pay-per-use only (the free tier and fixed Basic/Pro plans are gone), so every post or user your agent reads and every post it writes draws down prepaid credits. Following, liking and quote-posting via the API were removed from self-serve plans in April 2026.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create the app, set OAuth 2.0 settings, buy credits, then run the PKCE flow. No approval step is described.

timeToProd.assumes: An OAuth 2.0 user-context app on pay-per-use credits that reads and writes the connected user's posts. There's no review on any path. Volumes above 3M post reads a month need Enterprise.
timeToProd.waitingOn: No review needed. You need a funded credit balance, or requests are blocked.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: X's developer-app docs describe no review or approval process. The pricing page says requests are blocked when the balance runs out.

verdict.cost: Pay-per-use credits, bought upfront. Reads: $0.005 per post, $0.010 per user or DM event, $0.001 for owned reads of the app owner's own data. Writes: $0.015 per post, $0.20 per post with a URL. Capped at 3M post reads per month, then Enterprise (pricing on request).

prerequisites.item: An X account signed in to the Developer Console (console.x.com)
prerequisites.why: Apps, keys and credits are managed there. developer.x.com/en/portal now redirects to an X login.

prerequisites.item: A saved payment method and a credit balance
prerequisites.why: Pay-per-use draws down prepaid credits, and requests are blocked when the balance hits zero or the spending limit is reached.

prerequisites.item: HTTPS callback URLs (http://127.0.0.1 for local dev)
prerequisites.why: Callbacks must exactly match the allowlist (up to 10 per app), including trailing slashes. 'localhost' isn't the recommended host.

scopeTiers.impact: Sign in and read the user's profile. The token lasts 2 hours unless you add offline.access for a refresh token. X staff have said login endpoints are free under pay-per-use, but we couldn't confirm that.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The 'login is free' claim comes from a forum reply that returned 403 to our fetch, so it's unverified.

scopeTiers.tier: Read the user's data (billed per resource)
scopeTiers.impact: Read timelines, mentions, bookmarks, followers and DMs. Each returned resource costs credits ($0.005 per post, $0.010 per user or DM event). Owned reads cost $0.001, but only when the user owns the developer app.
Post ($0.015, or $0.20 with a URL), send DMs ($0.015) and upload media. The OAuth 1.0a app permission has to include write or DMs. Changing it forces users to re-authorize.
Following, liking and quote-posting via the API were removed from all self-serve tiers as of April 2026, even though the scopes still appear in the scope table.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Whether Enterprise customers keep these actions wasn't stated.

steps.title: Sign in to the Developer Console
steps.detail: Go to console.x.com with the X account that will own the app (it launched in February 2026, replacing the old developer portal).

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: console.x.com returned HTTP 200. developer.x.com/en/portal/dashboard returned 307 to an X login. We did not sign in.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Click Create App and enter a name, description and use case. Save the generated keys right away, since they're shown once. Consider separate apps for dev and prod.

steps.title: Configure user authentication settings
steps.detail: Set the app type to Web App (confidential, gets a client secret), set the OAuth 1.0a permission level (Read / Read+Write / Read+Write+DMs), and add exact callback URLs.

steps.title: Fund credits and set spend controls
steps.detail: Save a card, buy credits, and set auto-recharge and a per-cycle spending limit. New accounts can earn one-time promo credits ($20 for a first card plus a match of the first auto-recharge up to $50), which expire after 3 months.

steps.title: Pick minimal scopes and estimate cost
steps.detail: Map each agent feature to scopes and to per-resource prices. Model monthly cost per active user, keeping in mind the 24 h UTC dedup window and the 3M post-read cap.

steps.title: Implement OAuth 2.0 with PKCE
steps.detail: Redirect to https://x.com/i/oauth2/authorize with response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state and code_challenge (S256). Exchange the code within 30 seconds at POST https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token using Basic auth.

steps.title: Handle token refresh
steps.detail: Request offline.access. Access tokens expire after 2 hours. Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token and store whatever refresh token comes back.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Whether refresh tokens rotate or expire wasn't stated on the page.

steps.title: Add rate-limit and balance handling
steps.detail: Read the x-rate-limit-* headers, back off on 429 (code 88), and surface balance-depleted errors. Track usage via GET /2/usage/tweets.

steps.title: Optional: migrate stored OAuth 1.0a tokens
steps.detail: Since September 2026, POST /2/oauth2/token supports a token-exchange grant that turns OAuth 1.0a user tokens into OAuth 2.0 access and refresh tokens without re-authorization.

Configure the app type, permissions and callbacks
Add a payment card, buy credits and set spending limits

blockers.symptom: Requests blocked even though tokens are valid
blockers.cause: The credit balance is zero or negative, or the per-cycle spending limit has been hit.
blockers.fix: Add credits or raise the limit. Enable auto-recharge, which fires at most every 5 minutes and needs a default payment method.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange fails with an invalid code
blockers.cause: The authorization code expires 30 seconds after your app receives it.
blockers.fix: Exchange the code immediately in the callback handler.

blockers.cause: The redirect_uri doesn't exactly match the allowlist (trailing slash, localhost vs 127.0.0.1).
blockers.fix: Register the exact URL, using http://127.0.0.1 for local dev.

blockers.symptom: Follow, like or quote-post calls fail
blockers.cause: These actions were removed from all self-serve tiers in April 2026.
blockers.fix: Remove the features, or ask about Enterprise access.

blockers.cause: Per-user 15-minute limits (for example 75 for /2/users/me, 100 posts per 15 min, 300 for recent search).
blockers.fix: Wait until x-rate-limit-reset and spread calls out per user.

blockers.symptom: Users lose write or DM access after you change app permissions
blockers.cause: Changing the app permission level requires users to re-authorize to get new tokens.
blockers.fix: Pick the final permission level before launch, or prompt users to reconnect.

nuances.text: X's Developer Agreement (June 2025) bars using the X API or X Content 'to fine-tune or train a foundation or frontier model'. Using data at inference time isn't covered by that clause, but check the full agreement.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Quoted via TechCrunch. The agreement page returned HTTP 402 to our fetch.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 2 hours. Refresh tokens are only issued with offline.access, and the user stays connected until they revoke access.
Billing is per returned resource, with a soft 24-hour UTC dedup (a resource isn't charged twice in the same UTC day). Rate limits are separate from billing.
The cheap 'owned reads' price ($0.001) only applies when the authenticated user owns the developer app, so it doesn't help a multi-user agent reading its customers' data.
Spending through pay-per-use earns 10–20% back as xAI API credits if you link an xAI team.
